segs: READY FOR LIFE
DEVOTIONAL ON THE SURRENDERED LIFE BY CAROLYN RAYE
Ready for life after college? This is a 21-Day Devotional on seeking
God’s will in life decisions.

Ready to Know
Day Nine
Living for His glory
MEDITATE: “But may it never be that I should boast, except in the cross of
our Lord Jesus Christ…”
Galatians 6.14
READ: Galatians 6.11-15 (Ephesians 2:8-9)
Do you live by grace? Try this experiment:
Let’s say your morning begins with a great QT and
extended prayer time. A person in your class tells you that
they have been thinking about spiritual things and wanted to
know what you think. How would you feel about sharing
your faith?
Now let’s say, you woke up late this morning,
missed your QT and had a critical attitude all morning. You
go to class and the person asks you about spiritual things.
Would you feel differently or less comfortable about sharing
your faith? Why?
What does this experiment tell you about whether you live
by grace or by your works?
When you talk about ministry, are you more likely to start
by speaking of God’s remarkable work in your life and min-
istry or are you more likely to begin by talking about your-
self?
Verse 15 essentially says that it is not what we do or what
we do not do that matters, but what matters is what God
has done in making us a new creation. How does this give
you freedom? How does it warm your heart to the Savior?
THINK: To think that God will love you more for what you do, or
that you can have a greater standing before God because of what you
do, is to boast in your works, not in the cross. Likewise when we
think that our gifts, talents, and abilities is what is making our Bible
study or ministry successful is also to boast in our flesh. How can
you boast in God’s grace in your life and ministry?
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?
Ready to Know
Day Ten
Laying up treasures in Heaven
MEDITATE: “For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.”
Matthew 6:21
READ: Matthew 6:19-24 (Luke 12:16-21)
Where are the two places that you can lay up treasures for
yourself? What happens to the treasures in each place?
Think of someone you know who has placed heavenly val-
ues over earthly values and vice versa. What is it that you see
in their lives to let you know where their treasures (and thus,
their hearts) lie?
What are some indicators that someone your age is laying up
treasures on earth?
What are some indicators that someone your age is laying up
treasures in heaven?
THINK: As you think about college graduation, what occupies your
dreams and thoughts the most? (Success, significance, making
money, gaining possessions, status, prestige, serving God, loving
others, making an eternal impact?) Would you say that your
thoughts revolve more around storing up earthly treasures or heav-
enly treasures? What factors have caused you to think this way?
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?

Ready to Know
Day Eleven
Walking the path to true contentment
MEDITATE: “But godliness actually is a means of great gain, when accom-
panied by contentment.”
1 Timothy 6:6
READ: 1 Timothy 6:6-19 (2 Timothy 4:7)
What warnings are given about things to avoid in our pur-
suit of godliness? What reasons are given for avoiding such
snares?
What actions help us to ‘fight the good fight of faith’? What
attitudes help us to lay a ‘good foundation for the future’?
Knowing yourself, what temptations do you need to avoid
in order to ‘fight the good fight of faith’?
What principle in this passage, if applied to your life, would
cause you to be more content in life? How can you live out
that principle in the next few years?
THINK: What is it that you really want out of life? When you
think in the category of “things money can’t buy” what are some of
the most important things to you? How can you pursue those
dreams and desires in each of the career options before you?
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?
Ready to Know
Day Eight
Living for Others
WEEK TWO MEMORY VERSE: “But seek first His Kingdom and
His righteousness and all these things shall be added to you.”
Matthew 6:33
READ: Philippians 2:3-4 and Hebrews 10:24-25
How would you sum up what our attitude toward other
people ought not to be? Ought to be?
How do these instructions help us to live in humility as well
as follow Christ’s example of how to live for others?
From the Hebrews passage, what can we do to live for oth-
ers?
Is there someone in your life who could use your encour-
agement toward “love and good deeds” or toward living for
Christ? Who and what can you do to help them?
How does it affect your life when you gather together with
other believers? What would happen if there were long pe-
riods of time when you were not gathered with other believ-
ers?
THINK:
bered?
At the end of your life, what do you want the “other peo-
ple” in your life to say about you? How would you like to be remem-

Ready to Hear
Day Seven
Keeping an eternal perspective
MEDITATE: “Since you have been raised with Christ, set your hearts on
things above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.” Colossians 3:1
READ: Colossians 3:1-4 (Matthew 6:33)
Chapter 3 begins by addressing those who have been raised
up with Christ. This means that believers have been
brought to life spiritually through Jesus and that in Him
many things are true of us. Make a list of all the things that
Colossians says is true of you ‘in Him’, ‘through Him’, and
‘with Him’ (read also 3:3). How does this warm your heart
to the Savior?
Our response to these things is to set our hearts and minds
on things above, not on earthly things. What are the earthly
things that tend to capture your heart and/or captivate your
mind?
‘Setting your heart’ suggests striving after heavenly things and
‘setting your mind’ suggests concentrating on them. How does
concentrating on the things Colossians says is eternally true of
you motivate and give you boldness to strive after eternally
significant things?
THINK: C.T. Studd said, “If Jesus Christ be God and died for me,
then no sacrifice can be too great for me to make for Him.” Verse 4
ends with a reminder that since the ‘in Him’, ‘through Him’ and ‘with
Him’ things are true of us, that we will be with Him in glory. Eternal
perspective involves seeing yourself as you are seen in heaven and
pursuing heavenly things. How would your desires, dreams, and
beliefs change if you were to set your heart and mind on these
things?
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?
Ready to Know
Day Twelve
Examining the Greatest Commandments
MEDITATE: “By this all men will know that you are My disciples, if you
have love for one another.”
John 13:35
READ: Mark 12:30-31 (Revelation 3:15-16; John 13:34, 35)
How are we to love God? How are we to love others?
Why, out of the hundreds of commandments in the Old
Testament, do you think that Jesus said these were the two
greatest commandments? How do these “sum up the whole
law”?
What can compete for your love for God? What can cause
you to be “lukewarm” as described in Revelation 3:16?
What is an unselfish act that you can do in order to show
love to someone else this week?
THINK: These commandments apply to all believers, regardless of
their vocation. As you consider the career options before you, ask
yourself, ‘how will I be able to love God and love others’ as Jesus
commanded. How well will you be able to live out this command?
How could you be hindered in living out this command?
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?

Ready to Know
Day Thirteen
Praying for workers in the harvest
MEDITATE: “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.”
Matthew 9:37
READ: Matthew 9:36-38 (John 4:34-35)
What caused Jesus to feel compassion?
What do you think He was “seeing” as He looked at the
multitudes?
What was the specific instruction that Jesus gave to the dis-
ciples about what they were seeing?
What stirs your heart to feel compassion for other people?
When was the last time you had a unique experience of see-
ing someone through God’s eyes? What did it cause you to
do or to feel?
Will you take a moment and pray for “workers” to help
reach the people groups that you feel the most compassion
for?
THINK: How often do you think about being a ‘worker in the har-
vest’ in whatever job you have after college? Given the opportunities
before you, how could you be a ‘worker in the harvest’ in each set-
ting?
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?
Ready to Hear
Day Six
Knowing I am His son/daughter
MEDITATE: “Therefore you are no longer a slave, but a son; and if a son,
then an heir through God.”
Galatians 4:7
READ: Galatians 4:4-7 (Romans 8:12-17)
What are some of the differences in how a slave and a son
respond to the head of the house? As you think about obe-
dience to the Lord, do you interact with Him more as a son
or a slave?
Our Father deeply desires that we relate to Him as children,
who are free to obey and love Him and not as slaves who
fearfully labor for one who does not want their hearts, but
only their work. How does meditating on your sonship in
Christ warm your heart to the Savior?
Have you ever meditated on how big of a deal it is that you
are God’s son/daughter? Consider Ephesians 2:1-10.
There is a huge difference between who we were before
Christ and who we are now. It was not enough for God to
save us in our rebellion against Him. He also made us His
children.
God also makes us His heirs. What does this mean? What
are we heirs of?
THINK: You are a child of the Most High God! You no longer
have to live as a slave to sin (because you are saved) nor are you a
slave to God, since you are His son. How does knowing you are His
son give you security and rest? How does it motivate you for a life
of obedience? How would your sonship enable you to make bold
decisions about your life?
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?

Ready to Hear
Day Five
Believing that He knows me
MEDITATE: “O Lord, Thou has searched me and known me.”
Psalm 139:1
READ: Psalm 139:1-16 (Ephesians 2:10)
What does the Psalmist claim that God knows about him?
How does he respond to that realization?
What does God know about you?
Will you thank Him now for all that He knows about you,
including your past, the path of your life so far, and the way
the he made your physical body? (be specific)
THINK: Nothing about your life has escaped God’s notice. The
events, circumstances and emotions of your life are all known by
God. Are you willing to thank Him for both the good and the bad
and allow Him to use those things for His will and His glory no mat-
ter what you do after college?
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?
Ready to Know
Day Fourteen
Knowing God’s Heart for the Nations
MEDITATE: “Let the nations be glad and sing for joy…” Psalm 67.4
READ: Psalm 67 (Romans 10:12-16)
Psalm 67 talks a lot about the nations praising God, being
glad, and singing for joy. When you think of worshipping
the Lord, what things are you most thankful for?
John Piper suggests that missions exist because worship of
God does not. In other words missions exist to bring wor-
ship to people who cannot worship or be glad, for they have
no Savior. What would your life be like if you had no cause
to worship? If you had no Savior?
How does it make you feel to know that God uses His peo-
ple as His means to bring worship to the nations? Read
Romans 10.12-16. Who brought you to worship the Lord?
THINK: God’s heart for missions begins with His desire to be glo-
rified throughout the world. God is glorified when we worship Him
with our lips, our actions, and our lives and when we take our wor-
ship to nations that do not know the name of Jesus. Thus missions
is worship. Have you ever thought of missions as an act of worship?
What would it be like to see a person in another country who has
never heard the name of Jesus worship Him for the very first time?
Let the nations be glad!
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?

Ready to Act
Day Fifteen
Trusting His ways
WEEK THREE MEMORY VERSE:
“Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice.”
1 Samuel 15:22
READ: Proverbs 3:5-6 (Judges 6 & 7)
What are we told to DO in this passage?
NOT to do?
What are we told
While this sounds so simple, living it out can be more diffi-
cult. Why is that?
Read the story of Gideon in Judges 6:11-7:23. How did
Gideon follow God’s ways instead of His own? What do
you think was going on in His heart as this story unfolded?
What were the results of obeying God’s ways?
Has there been a time that you followed God’s ways even
when though it went against your own understanding?
What happened?
THINK: What if God asked you to do something that didn’t make
sense to you or to those around you? How would you feel? What
would you do? As you pray about your future, are you sincerely try-
ing to follow God’s ways? Or do you find yourself, at times, wanting
God to approve of the path you have planned out?
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?
Ready to Hear
Day Four
Renewing my mind
MEDITATE: “Whom do I have in heaven but You? And the earth has
nothing I desire besides You.”
Psalm 73:25
READ: Psalm 73 (Romans 12:1-2)
How does the Psalmist describe his perspective and attitude
(73.1-5; 13-14)? What is his perspective and attitude to-
wards the wicked who surround him (73.6-12)?
Can you think of a time when you have had a crisis of faith
(when your foot almost slipped)? What brought you out of
it?
The turning point of the Psalm is in vv. 15-17 when the
Psalmist meets with God. From this point until the end of
the Psalm, his perspective changes and he begins to perceive
things rightly, from God’s perspective. How has meeting
with the Lord corrected your own perspectives, revealed
your sin (vv. 21-22), or changed the way that you perceive
the world, the wicked, and yourself?
THINK: God is our creator and sovereign Lord. He is blind to
nothing and even when bad things happen, we can have confidence
that He is in control. When we see the wicked prosper or other
things that make no sense to us, we must take comfort in God’s
word and do our best to know His perspective. When you see life
played out in front of you, do you interpret it in light of God’s word?
When you feel hopeless, where do you turn in God’s word to bring
you comfort? As you look towards life after college, do you see it
through a Biblical grid?
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?

Day Three
Keeping a clean heart
MEDITATE: “I acknowledged my sin to Thee, and my iniquity I did not
hide; I said, “I will confess my transgressions to the Lord”; And Thou didst
forgive the guilt of my sin.”
Psalm 32:5
READ: Psalm 32: 1-7 (Psalm 51)
How does the Psalmist describe the effects of sin in his own
life?
Holding on to sin not only affects us spiritually, but also
physically, emotionally and relationally. How have you seen
those affects of sin in your own life? Think of a specific
example.
What steps would you take to “acknowledge” and “confess”
your sin? Describe a time in the past few years when you
experienced the weight of sin lifted from you.
If there is any sin in your life today that is hindering your
relationship and communication with God, will you confess
it and make things right?
THINK: How would sin --- something you’ve done or an attitude
that you’re holding on to --- affect your ability to hear from God as
you pray about His will for your life after college? As you seek to
have a clean heart before God, consider areas of your life such as
lust, selfishness, materialism, greed, unforgiveness, holding grudges,
demanding your own way, worry, impurity or immorality, etc. How
could sin in one of these areas of your life be hindering you from
hearing clearly from God?
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?
Ready to Act
Day Sixteen
Using the talents He has given me
MEDITATE: “As each one has received a special gift, employ it in serving
one another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.”
1 Peter 4:10
READ: Matthew 25:14-30 (1 Peter 4:10-11)
What does the Master expect of those that He has entrusted
His possessions to?
What character qualities and actions does the Master praise?
What has God entrusted to you? (gifts, talents, experiences,
etc.)
How have you used the “talents” that God has given you
during your college years? Would you hear “well done,
good and faithful servant” from the Master? Why or why
not?
THINK: You have a unique heritage, spiritual journey, personality
and gifts. Have you considered how each of those factors can play
into your career decisions?
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?

Day Seventeen
Stepping out of my comfort zone
MEDITATE: “And he said, “Behold, Here am I, Lord.” Acts 9:10b
READ: Acts 9:10-19 (1 Samuel 3)
What was Ananias’ heart response toward God in verse 10?
How did it change as God revealed his ‘assignment’ for
him?
What happened as a result of Ananias’ obedience? How
could an experience like that change your life?
Has God ever prompted you, or led you, to do something
that made you want to say “I object!”? If so, what was the
result of either your obedience or your disobedience?
THINK:
Obedience brings blessing. If God were to lead you to
do something that is not currently on your ‘list of options’, how
might you respond? Are you ready and willing to obey as you seek
God’s will for your life?

Day Two
Valuing and honoring His Word
MEDITATE: “Thy testimonies also are my delight; They are my counselors.”
Psalm 119:24
READ: Psalm 119:33-38 (Psalm 1:1-3)
What are all the things that the Psalmist asks for?
Why are these the things that he wants from the Lord?
When you pray, what are the things you are most likely to
ask for yourself?
How would you rate your desire to know God’s word so that

situation, rarely think about it)
THINK: Do you see God’s word as a guide in helping you make a
career decision? Are you being diligent to read and study the Bible?
Do you value the counsel of God’s word over the counsel of your
family and friends? Why or why not?

Day One
Seeing Him as my good shepherd
WEEK ONE MEMORY VERSE: “Search me, O God, and know my
heart; Try me and know my anxious thought; And see if there be any hurtful
way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.”
READ: Psalm 23 (John 10:11, 14)
What does a shepherd do for his sheep?
As a shepherd, what does God do for His sheep?
What are the most significant times that you have seen God
as your shepherd (comforting, leading, guiding, protecting)
you during your college years?
Do you honestly see God as your good shepherd now? If
so, what has contributed to you following Him in this way?
If not, what prevents you from truly seeing Him as your
shepherd?
THINK: In order to look to God for His wisdom in what to do
after college, you must believe that He CAN and that He WILL lead
you in the best way. Can you trust Him with your life in that way?
Be honest and list out the fears you have in trusting God to lead you
in your career decisions.
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?

Having confidence in God’s Promises
MEDITATE: “And without faith it is impossible to please Him, for he who
comes to God must believe that He is, and that He is a rewarder of those who
seek Him.” Hebrews 11:6
READ: Numbers 13 and 14:6-10 (Hebrews 11:6)
Why did God instruct Moses to send spy’s into the land?
What factors made ten of the spies report the impossibility
of this feat?
What caused Joshua and Caleb to have a different conclu-
sion even though they saw the same things as the other ten
spies?
After all that the Israelites had been through, they were on
the brink of blessing. What would they have needed to do
in order to receive that blessing?
THINK: As you think about your future, is there something that
you would really love to do if there just weren’t so many barriers in
the way? What is that? Do you sense that God is leading you in
those dreams? What are the barriers that stand in the way? What are
some promises that God gives to deal with each of those barriers?
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?

Ready to Act
Day Nineteen
Asking for wisdom
“But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God.”
James 1:5
READ: James 1:2-8 (Philippians 4:6-7)
What instructions are we given in this passage (our part)?
What is true about God in this passage (His part)?
Why do you think there is such strong instruction about
asking for wisdom and not doubting that God will give it?
Describe the difference between ‘praying with confidence’
and ‘praying with doubts’. Which one would best describe
your prayers? Why?
What are the specific things that you need wisdom about
today? Have you seen Him give you wisdom in the past
when you had a big decision before you? Describe that
situation.
THINK: When you pray about your future, do you really believe
that God will guide you? What are you praying for? Is it specific?
Will you know when it has been answered?
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?
Prayer.
A relationship with God involves communication — telling
God what is on our hearts, making requests and taking the time to
listen and hear back from Him. James 1:5 says that if any of us lacks
wisdom, to ask God. Philippians 4:6-7 tells us to let our requests be
known. Spending time in prayer causes us to align our will with His
will. Do your prayers involve both sincere asking and quiet lis-
tening?
Wise Counselors.
Those who have gone before you have learned many valu-
able lessons. Their insights, if guided by the Holy Spirit, can be of
great help in your decision making. Are your ‘counselors’ advising
you from a biblical perspective?
Circumstances and Desires.
We often stand amazed at how God works in our circum-
stances and even changes our heart’s desire. These are powerful fac-
tors in making a decision, especially when experienced in conjunction
with all the principles listed above. However, circumstances and
desires, when isolated from the previous principles, can easily be mis-
leading. Are you giving the proper “weight “ to how circum-
stances and desires are driving your decisions?
A Process.
The combination of all these things will help lead you in
making the BEST decisions. But this is not a fast process, not a one-
time prayer or one quiet time. To take all these principles into con-
sideration will require time and patience. Using this guide will help
give you some tracks to run on as you seek God for His direction for
your life.

Principles for Seeking
God’s Will
Master. Mate. Mission. These three major decisions will end
up defining most of your life. Once we have established that God is
indeed our Master, then the matter of our mate and mission becomes
of utmost importance. These two decisions often lead us to asking
“what is God’s will” more than any other decisions in life.
The following principles and questions will also help you in
this process.
Ask the right question.
While it is natural, in our human state and in our American
culture, to ask “what is God’s will for me?”, perhaps a better ques-
tion is “How do I fit into God’s will?” He has a sovereign plan for
the whole world. Do you want to fit into His overall plan, or do
you want Him to fit into your plans?
A yielded life.
When seeking God’s will, it usually revolves around a spe-
cific decision that we are uncertain about. Before we seek God for
the future, we need to make sure that we are submitting to God’s will
in the present. Is He Lord of your life? Lord of your will? Are you
presently doing all the things that you do know to be God’s
will?
Guidance from God’s Word.
In the scriptures, we see many ways that God spoke — au-
dibly, visions, revelations, prophets, etc. Today, though we have the
full revealed will of God given to us in the scriptures. His word con-
tains principles to guide our whole lives, not just isolated decisions
that we will face at various times in life. Are you consistently read-
ing and studying God’s Word?
Ready to Act
Day Twenty
Giving Him my heart
MEDITATE: “But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his
face, because he stood condemned.”
Galatians 2:11
READ: Galatians 2:11-14 (John 12:43)
What comes to your mind when you think about idolatry?
Most of the time we think of pagan primitives bowing down
to wood or stone idols that they made in their spare time.
However, there is much more to the idea of idolatry. One
pastor defines idols as, “Anything we believe apart from
Christ to make us happy, satisfied, or fulfilled.” Think on
this quote for a minute. Write down your immediate
thoughts.
Peter used to hang out over meals with his Gentile buddies.
But when some of his hotshot Jewish friends came into
town, he began to change his lunch plans since he did not
want to be seen hanging out with ‘unclean’ Gentiles. At this
instant, Peter began to care more for his popularity and ap-
proval than the gospel.
Idols arise when we desire something more than we desire
Jesus, put our trust in anything other than God, or serve any
other thing rather than our Lord. You can see this in Peter’s
life, how have you seen this in yours?
THINK: Generally, there are 4 things that can steal our hearts from
God. When they do we begin to obey them more than the Lord and
make decisions in light of them rather than making decisions in faith.
They are: seeking comfort (fear of stress, demands), seeking approval
(fear of rejection), seeking control (fear of uncertainty), and seeking
power (fear of humiliation). Which do you struggle with? How can
you replace it with faith in God?
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?

Ready to Act
Day Twenty-one
Being a blessing to others
MEDITATE: “God be gracious to us and bless us, and cause His face to
shine upon us, that Your way may be known on earth, Your salvation among the
nations.” Psalm 67
READ: Psalm 67
Consider all the things that you consider to be the Lord’s
blessing in your life. Why do you think that the Lord has
blessed you so richly in so many ways?
The first two verses of this psalm are very interesting. The
psalmist is asking God’s blessing not for himself, but so he
might be a blessing to others! Have you ever prayed like the
psalmist that God would bless you so that you would have
more to give?
The reason the psalmist asked God to shine His face upon
them and give them His favor was so God’s way would be
known and salvation would be among the nations. God’s
glory and the expansion of God’s kingdom were the focal
points of his asking for blessing. When you pray for God’s
blessings in your life, how could you begin to pray in a way
that focused more on your blessing being for the nations
and less for yourself?
THINK: What are the blessings God has given you and how could
they be used to expand His glory to the nations? What could you
begin to do now to develop a lifetime practice of blessing the nations
with the things God gives you? Think of God’s gifts of time, fi-
nances, and your talents/abilities. Consider how God’s blessings in
these categories could be given to advance His kingdom.
WRITE: What is God saying to you today?
Using This Devotional Guide
While most of you probably really want to know God’s will
and want to do what He leads you to do, the process involved can
seem so mysterious or vague, that it is just easier to utilize quicker or
easier methods of making a decision.
This devotional guide has been written with you in mind to
help you prepare your heart in seeking the Lord for His guidance in
making your career decisions.
Week One —– Ready to Hear
This week’s focus will be on examining your own heart con-
dition. You will be preparing your heart to be able to hear from
God.
Week Two —– Ready to Know
This week’s focus will be on knowing God’s heart and
thinking like God thinks. You will be gaining an eternal perspective
to guide you in your decision making.
Week Three — Ready to Act
This week’s focus will be on following God in faith and
obedience. You will be learning biblical truths about the blessings
and consequences of your actions.

Dear Graduating Senior,
As a student involved with Campus Crusade for Christ, you
have had the opportunity to experience God working in your life and
through your life. Hopefully, you are a ‘changed person’, not the

As you wrestle with the choices before you of ‘what to do
after college graduation’, we would like to challenge you to sincerely
go before God and patiently wait to hear from Him about His will
for your life upon college graduation.

guide for 21 days to prepare your heart to pray for God’s guidance.
Second, we are asking that you find a prayer partner and
pray for 30 days about all the choices that are before you when you
graduate.
